sampling_model.design: Two-arm predictable sequential randomization through recruitment time \(T\), with known logged propensities, deterministic lower-envelope quotas, and records observed through the prespecified terminal time \(H_T=T+\Delta_T\).
sampling_model.units: One independent and identically distributed potential outcome-delay vector arrives at each integer recruitment time \(t\leq T\); each revealed assigned response records its calendar revelation time and realized delay.
sampling_model.treatment: The prespecified rare arm has probability between \(ct^{-\alpha}\) and \(Ct^{-\alpha}\), with \(0<c\leq C\leq1-\varepsilon<1\). In the two-arm simplex, the upper rare-arm envelope implies \(\pi_t(0)\geq1-C\geq\varepsilon\); an explicit control floor is imposed only on the separate one-sided comparison class.
sampling_model.overlap: The novel two-sided polynomial comparability regime fixes the rare-arm information order at \(T^{1-\alpha}\); the one-sided forced-exploration class is retained separately for achievability comparison.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No delay law or outcome regression is estimated. The procedure uses terminally observable fixed-age indicators, sample variances, a known tail envelope, and an observable variance gate.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their estimator converges to a normal distribution under appropriate conditions.
The observed empirical mean is no longer an unbiased estimator of the expected reward.
They only assume that there is a bound on the tail of the delay.
With bounded or sub-Gaussian reward distributions, the upper bounds are optimal with a matching lower bound.
Maximum likelihood estimators from such a trial have the usual asymptotic properties.
The adaptively-weighted estimator is consistent, and the studentized statistic is asymptotically normal.
Their stabilized estimator is asymptotically normal under consistent conditional-standard-deviation estimation.
They derive finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds under normal errors with known variance.
Their central limit theorem enables semiparametrically efficient inference at fixed sample sizes.
They derive the efficient influence function under propensities bounded away from zero and one.

body.tldr: A two-arm adaptive experiment with a rare arm sampled at a probability comparable to \(t^{-\alpha}\) and an outcome-dependent delay tail bounded by \(L(1+u)^{-\beta}\) admits uniformly honest intervals for the eventual mean contrast with minimax expected length \(\max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\}\) after prespecified follow-up \(\Delta_T\); at end of recruitment this is \(\max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},T^{-\beta}\}\). The observed record includes revelation times, so shifted main and old cohort windows are measurable and added follow-up changes the statistic. An observable variance gate splices a bias-aware Gaussian interval to a concentration fallback, and the vanishing tail-envelope-to-standard-error ratio is the boundary for a protocol-level ordinary-Wald guarantee over the full class, although prompt-delay laws can validate ordinary Wald pointwise. Every expected interval length averages over the outcome-delay arrivals and any randomization induced by the predictable adaptive design policy.

project_justification.gap: Delayed adaptive-inference theory centers scores by imposing outcome-delay independence and typically assumes only a forced-exploration floor, whereas reward-dependent-delay theory establishes regret bounds and selection-bias constructions rather than uniformly honest confidence intervals.
project_justification.niche: The unresolved niche is finite-horizon inference for an eventual causal contrast when exploration is two-sided comparable to a vanishing schedule, revelation is informative, the allocation scaling need not converge, and post-recruitment follow-up changes the observed endpoint set.
project_justification.fill: The project combines a revelation-time-complete observed-law arm-tape reduction, deterministic shifted two-cohort prefixes, a uniform variance gate, and same-policy hidden-tail alternatives to deliver the rate frontier, the Wald boundary, and a clinical follow-up rule.

body.related_work: Shi, Wang, and Wu provide the closest delayed adaptive-inference setup and impose a one-sided polynomial forced-exploration condition; that condition is used here only for the separate achievability reduction, while their formal centering also uses outcome-delay independence. The two-sided comparability condition is a novel design regime: its lower envelope guarantees enough rare-arm observations for the upper construction, whereas its upper envelope prevents the policy class from silently supplying more rare-arm information and is required for the matching same-experiment converse. Hadad et al. and Bibaut et al. supply predictable AIPW weighting and conditional-variance stabilization for prompt outcomes. Manegueu et al. supply the polynomial delay-tail envelope under reward-delay independence. Lancewicki et al. and Tang, Wang, and Zheng show how reward-dependent delays bias observed rewards and construct regret lower bounds; they inform the hidden-tail decomposition rather than serve as interval comparators. Bai, Hu, and Rosenberger establish classical response-adaptive asymptotics with response-dependent delays. Armstrong and Kolesár provide the bounded-bias Gaussian calibration adapted here. Ma, Wang, and Wei derive delayed CARA efficiency under conditional delay-outcome independence and nonvanishing allocation. Liberali et al. provide the cardiovascular-trial consumer and document inferior-arm precision costs in simulations, without a theorem-level coverage guarantee under outcome-dependent ascertainment; the resulting tail-pad or follow-up requirement is therefore a protocol-level condition for uniform validity over the envelope class, not a claim that every individual trial law invalidates ordinary Wald.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The minimax order has a concentration and two-point route, but the single-procedure claim depends on a uniform studentized approximation at the observable \(1/\log T\) gate. The proof must control the overlap between \(M_{a,\Delta}\) and \(U_{a,\Delta}\), the random sample variance near the gate, and quota-failure conventions without conditioning. The generic radius \(B_{T,\Delta}\) is a class-wide tail envelope rather than the actual bias \(b_{T,\Delta}\); it can remain positive for a prompt-delay law whose actual bias is zero. Exact expected-length constants over randomized or variable-length intervals are not claimed. The model excludes unknown tail envelopes, cross-arrival dependence, and nonstationary endpoint rates; permanent nonrevelation is excluded by the polynomial envelope with \(\beta>0\), not by a separate assumption.
body.honest_scope: The arm-tape equivalence, quota concentration, shifted old-tail variance calculation, and hidden-sign lower experiment are theorem targets supported by explicit proof routes but remain to be written rigorously. The uniform gate theorem is the principal open proof obligation. The ordinary-Wald boundary is asserted only for uniform honesty of the constructed \(\Delta_T\)-indexed fixed-quota statistic over regular variance subfamilies, not for arbitrary unweighted adaptive estimators or as a necessity statement for every individual law. The two-sided allocation envelope defines the exact frontier class; under the larger one-sided forced-exploration class only achievability is asserted. When delays are identically zero, the actual hidden-tail bias and old-cohort correction vanish and ordinary fixed-quota Wald inference is pointwise valid, while the unchanged generic envelope radius need not vanish numerically. Application to GUSTO-1 or EUROPA requires an external audit of stationarity, logged propensities, the endpoint-tail envelope, and the use of a risk-difference estimand.
